name: PySpark + Scala
desc: Spark processes data that doesn't fit on one machine. Every PySpark concept maps to something you already know from Python and SQL.
tip: Interviewers test Spark by asking why is this job slow. Know the answers: shuffles, collect() on large data, missing broadcast, data skew. The Spark UI shows all of these.

r: Pulls ALL data to the driver. Crashes on large data. Only collect small aggregated results.
Copies small table to every executor. Eliminates shuffling the large table.
One key has far more rows. One executor runs forever. Fix with salting.
cache()=memory only. persist(StorageLevel)=configurable. Both avoid recomputing.
Columnar, compressed, schema-aware. 10x+ faster for analytics.
BroadcastHashJoin=no shuffle. SortMergeJoin=shuffle. Check before running slow jobs.

parts.title: Spark architecture -- Driver, Executors, lazy evaluation
parts.summary: Every Spark performance question flows from understanding the Driver/Executor model and lazy evaluation. Understand this before writing a single line of code.

parts.title: DataFrames -- read, transform, write
parts.summary: The DataFrame API deliberately mirrors SQL and pandas. Key differences: laziness, Parquet output, and explicit schema for production.

parts.title: Joins, aggregations, broadcast -- performance fundamentals
parts.summary: Broadcast joins eliminate the most expensive shuffle in many pipelines. Understanding when Spark chooses broadcast vs sort-merge is where most Spark optimizatio…

parts.title: Window functions, caching, persistence
parts.summary: PySpark window functions use identical PARTITION BY / ORDER BY semantics as SQL -- vocabulary, not new concepts. Caching avoids recomputing expensive transforma…

parts.title: Performance -- skew, salting, partitioning, AQE
parts.summary: The answer to every slow Spark job is almost always: data skew, missing broadcast, too many shuffles, or wrong partition count.

parts.title: Scala basics for PySpark developers
parts.summary: Reading fluency only. Once you know PySpark, Scala Spark is mostly vocabulary. The JD mentions Scala so expect can-you-read-this questions.

parts.title: Production Spark -- EMR deployment, Spark UI, Structured Streaming
parts.summary: Reading the Spark UI is the difference between guessing at performance problems and diagnosing them.

parts.title: Spark Catalyst Optimizer & Adaptive Query Execution (AQE)
parts.summary: Deep-dive into Spark query planning: Unresolved Logical Plan → Analyzed → Optimized → Physical Plan, and AQE runtime optimizations.

parts.title: Data Lakehouse Architecture & Delta Lake Compaction
parts.summary: Senior data engineers must master Delta Lake ACID guarantees, Z-Ordering, Liquid Clustering, Time Travel, and VACUUM compaction.
